{{Short description|Concept in survey design}}
'''Mischievous responders''' are individuals—typically youth—who jokingly provide dishonest and extreme answers to [[Survey (human research)|survey]] questions. The impact of mischievous responders on data related to [[LGBTQ youth vulnerability|disparities between heterosexual and sexual minority youth]] has been noted, with studies finding that mischievous responders [[Response bias|distort data]] to overestimate disparities.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Robinson-Cimpian |first=Joseph P. |date=2014-05-01 |title=Inaccurate Estimation of Disparities Due to Mischievous Responders: Several Suggestions to Assess Conclusions |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.3102/0013189X14534297 |journal=Educational Researcher |language=EN |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=171–185 |doi=10.3102/0013189X14534297 |issn=0013-189X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> These distortions of data can sometimes lead to inaccuracies that "substantively affect research, policy, and public discourse regarding a variety of disparities".<ref name=":0" /> A 2019 [[Preregistration (science)|pre-registered study]] found data from mischievous responders to account for the entirety of numerous apparent disparities between heterosexuals and sexual minorities, including in [[heroin]] use and [[drunk driving]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Cimpian |first1=Joseph R. |last2=Timmer |first2=Jennifer D. |date=2019-10-01 |title=Large-Scale Estimates of LGBQ-Heterosexual Disparities in the Presence of Potentially Mischievous Responders: A Preregistered Replication and Comparison of Methods |journal=AERA Open |language=EN |volume=5 |issue=4 |article-number=2332858419888892 |doi=10.1177/2332858419888892 |issn=2332-8584|doi-access=free }}</ref> Mischievous responders are more often boys than girls, and tend to falsely report being [[lesbian]], [[Gay men|gay]], [[Bisexuality|bisexual]] or [[queer]].<ref name=":1" /> A 2006 study found that 99% of young respondents who'd claimed in a survey to have used an [[Artificial limbs|artificial limb]] were lying, as determined in follow-up interviews.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fan |first1=Xitao |last2=Miller |first2=Brent C. |last3=Park |first3=Kyung-Eun |last4=Winward |first4=Bryan W. |last5=Christensen |first5=Mathew |last6=Grotevant |first6=Harold D. |last7=Tai |first7=Robert H. |date=2006-08-01 |title=An Exploratory Study about Inaccuracy and Invalidity in Adolescent Self-Report Surveys |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/152822x06289161 |journal=Field Methods |language=EN |volume=18 |issue=3 |pages=223–244 |doi=10.1177/152822X06289161 |issn=1525-822X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Kamenetz |first=Anya |date=2014-05-22 |title='Mischievous Responders' Confound Research On Teens |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/ed/2014/05/22/313166161/mischievous-responders-confound-research-on-teens |access-date=2025-05-25 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref> Research suggests that mischievous responders are "ubiquitous in [[Adolescence|adolescent]] research using [[Self-report study|self-administered questionnaires]]".<ref name=":0" /> Methods for identifying and accounting for data from mischievous responders include the use of boosted regressions, and some surveys include questions with impossible answers to catch dishonest respondents. Others simply ask respondents if they had been honest.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cimpian |first1=Joseph R. |last2=Timmer |first2=Jennifer D. |last3=Birkett |first3=Michelle A. |last4=Marro |first4=Rachel L. |last5=Turner |first5=Blair C. |last6=Phillips |first6=Gregory L. |date=November 2018 |title=Bias From Potentially Mischievous Responders on Large-Scale Estimates of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, or Questioning (LGBQ)-Heterosexual Youth Health Disparities |journal=American Journal of Public Health |volume=108 |issue=S4 |pages=S258–S265 |doi=10.2105/AJPH.2018.304407 |issn=1541-0048 |pmc=6215371 |pmid=30383423}}</ref> The term "mischievous responders" was coined in 2011 by Joseph P. Robinson-Cimpian.<ref name=":2" />
